title: Automotive parts plant, second shift
summary: Luis, the second-shift maintenance tech, walks Cell 3 at the Arlington plant. He inherits a locked-out conveyor from first shift, chases a spindle overtemp on CNC-07 down to a kinked coolant hose, gets a spare from the tool crib, and has the machine cutting again within the hour; Priya, the cell lead, signs off the first piece. Late in the shift he finds a weeping fitting on press HP-2 and leaves it, and the conveyor, for third shift.
style: Unedited first-person snapshot from a head-mounted wearable camera at eye level, deep focus with everything sharp, no bokeh, on an industrial factory floor, slightly off-level framing, mixed overhead sodium and LED lighting, light sensor noise, realistic grime and wear, no faces in frame (a coworker's gloved hands at most).

issues.title: CV-3 drive belt worn, conveyor locked out until the replacement belt arrives
CNC-07 stopped on alarm 1012 spindle overtemp
HP-2 return-line fitting weeping hydraulic oil

shots.prompt: A whiteboard on the wall of a factory maintenance shop with neat block-capital marker writing: a header "2ND SHIFT", and below it the lines "CV-3 LOCKED OUT - BELT ON ORDER" and "PM: CMP-1 FILTER"; a workbench with tools and a parts bin in front of it.
shots.note: Start of shift. First shift left CV-3 locked out, belt is on order.

shots.prompt: Operator control screen of a CNC machining center, metal chips and coolant behind the window; a large plate above the screen reads "CNC-07"; the screen shows "RUNNING" in green and "SPINDLE 8000 RPM".
Round analog hydraulic pressure gauge on a large industrial press with the needle in the green band; a yellow stenciled label next to it reads "HP-2".
A roller conveyor with a red lockout padlock on its disconnect switch and a red tag reading "LOCKED OUT"; a stenciled sign on the conveyor frame reads "CV-3".
shots.note: CV-3 still locked out under WO-2207, Ray's lock and mine both on the disconnect.

shots.prompt: A machined aluminum part on a granite inspection table next to digital calipers and a printed inspection sheet with large text "LOT 2291 PASS".

Control panel of a large industrial rotary screw air compressor in a compressor room, seen from a step back; a big engraved plate reads "CMP-1"; the panel display shows "RUNNING" and "7.2 BAR" in large green text and only green indicator lights are lit; a new air filter cartridge in its box sits on top of the cabinet; no hands in frame.
shots.note: PM on CMP-1: intake filter changed, holding 7.2 bar.

shots.prompt: Operator control screen of a CNC machining center, metal chips and coolant behind the window; a large plate above the screen reads "CNC-07"; the screen shows a red banner "ALARM 1012 SPINDLE OVERTEMP".
shots.edit: change only the control screen so it shows a red banner reading "ALARM 1012 SPINDLE OVERTEMP" instead of RUNNING.
shots.note: Priya called me over: CNC-07 stopped mid-cycle on alarm 1012, spindle overtemp.

shots.prompt: Close-up inside the open side access panel of a CNC machining center, lit by a flashlight: a black rubber coolant hose is folded sharply into a tight V-shaped kink and crushed flat where it is pinched behind a steel bracket; a gloved finger points at the kink; a small engraved plate on the inside of the panel door reads "CNC-07".
shots.note: Found the cause: coolant hose kinked behind the bracket, no coolant flow to the spindle.

shots.prompt: Across a tool crib service counter with wire-mesh shelving behind it, a coworker's gloved hand slides a new coiled black coolant hose in a clear plastic bag across the counter; a printed white part label on the bag reads "44-118 COOLANT HOSE".
shots.note: Dana at the tool crib had a spare coolant hose, part 44-118.

shots.prompt: Operator control screen of a CNC machining center showing "RUNNING" in green, a plate above reads "CNC-07", and a yellow sticky note on the frame reads "HOSE REPLACED".
shots.edit: change only the control screen so it shows "RUNNING" in green and "SPINDLE 8000 RPM" like a normal running machine, and add a small yellow sticky note on the machine frame beside the screen with marker text "HOSE REPLACED".
shots.note: Replaced the coolant hose and rerouted it clear of the bracket. Alarm cleared, CNC-07 back to normal and cutting again.

shots.prompt: A freshly machined aluminum part on a granite inspection table with a digital height gauge beside it and a printed inspection sheet with large bold text "LOT 2292 FIRST PIECE PASS".
shots.note: First piece off CNC-07 after the repair measures in tolerance. Lot 2292 released.

shots.prompt: Looking down at the base of a large hydraulic press beside a big yellow stenciled marking "HP-2" on its frame; a hydraulic hose fitting is wet with oil and a small dark puddle of oil spreads on the concrete floor, partly soaked by a white absorbent pad; a bright yellow tag zip-tied to the fitting reads "OIL LEAK" in large black marker letters.
shots.note: HP-2 return-line fitting is weeping, small oil leak at the base. Pad down; needs a new fitting before it gets worse.

shots.prompt: A wall-mounted production status board at the end of a machining cell with large printed digits: "CELL 3", "PLAN 340", "ACTUAL 312", and "STOP MIN 43".
shots.note: Cell 3 at 312 of 340, the 43 minutes on CNC-07 cost us the rest.

shots.prompt: The same maintenance shop whiteboard, rewritten for the next shift.
shots.edit: change only the whiteboard writing: header "3RD SHIFT", then the lines "CV-3 LOCKED OUT - BELT TUE", "HP-2 FITTING WEEPING - PAD DOWN", and "CNC-07 HOSE DONE", in the same neat block-capital marker.
shots.note: Board updated for third shift: CV-3 belt Tuesday, HP-2 fitting still to do.
